title: US Ops playbook
subtitle: What we stand for, how we work, and how we decide. Pairs with the task grid.

story.label: Why we're here
story.mission: Run Your City is committed to building an inclusive community through the sport of running. We aim to provide every child, regardless of ability, gender or socioeconomic background, the opportunity to grow into healthy, confident, and inspired individuals.
story.brand_line: Where every kid is empowered to reach their starting line

values.t: Every child feels safe, seen, and celebrated
Movement is joyful, free, and for everyone
Every step is a chance to grow

items.t: Founded in 2018 in Charlottesville, Virginia by UVA student-athletes
Set a goal in 2024 to reach 10,000 kids by 2035

team.label: How US Ops works
team.owner: Owner = you make sure it happens and gets communicated. Pull in anyone for input. It can't slip silently.

owns: Sets direction and season goals
Owns everything that goes to all chapters, incl. the parent newsletter (kickoff, mid-season, wrap-up)
Runs the weekly ops call, kickoff and end-of-season calls
Owns info@runyourcity.org and safety incidents
Builds and runs leadership training
Celebrates impact at every level and empowers the team, every week
roles.escalates: Final call on US Ops decisions

owns: Runs the pipeline: interest calls and go/no-go
Assigns confirmed chapters to interns
Runs insurance, facility forms and invoices
Runs group calls when chapters share a problem
Owns us-ops@runyourcity.org, the playbook and chapter materials
Takes each assigned chapter start to finish
Locks location, dates and leadership team
Checks the session-one gate
Flags struggling chapters and wins
Makes sure leader handoffs happen
Finds priority schools and athletes
Sets up chapter accounts, web page and app
Runs automated check-ins and reminders
Sends automatic end-of-season emails

standards.t: Lock the weekly meeting time; cameras on
Reply to chapters within 48 hours (email or text)
No silent failures: flag it the moment something slips
A 'redshirt or graduate' path for anyone who can't meet the standards
Have fun and make this a fulfilling experience

items.t: Anything that goes to all chapters goes through the lead
Interns escalate to the coordinator; coordinators escalate to the lead
Chapters alert the lead about any safety incident right away
The owner decides and tells everyone affected; input is welcome, silence is not
The lead owns info@runyourcity.org; coordinators own us-ops@runyourcity.org
No more GroupMes; connect chapters across cohorts by email
Chapters reach US Ops by email and text; we reply within 48 hours
Before session one, check the gate: safety basics in place, leadership trained, handoff done. Then go live or push the start
If a season is pushed back: pause the chapter in the app, update the web page, email signups (copy info@runyourcity.org)
Don't cancel the insurance invoice if the chapter already started
Merge a chapter into a nearby one, or move a family, when that serves kids better
Flag struggling chapters and wins every week, so they get support or recognition
Red zone: a chapter with under 30 signups, or any parent complaint in the past month (month or week, to confirm)
How often we check in on red-zone chapters
Pause: a chapter that misses 2 key deadlines (choosing a location, setting the leadership team, selecting session dates), after being reminded 3+ times before each
Who decides a pause, who tells families, and how a chapter restarts
When to make exceptions, like late insurance

tracking.label: Meetings and follow-up

meetings.t: Weekly US Ops call: fixed time, 30 minutes, everyone brings 3 to 5 chapters, written recap after
Group calls when several chapters hit the same problem
Chapter kickoff call and parent welcome meeting

tracking.proposal_title: Proposal: task tracker and how we track ownership

proposal.t: Every task on the grid has one owning role; the owner sets a date
Every action item from a meeting goes in the recap with an owner and a date
Open items roll into one tracker and get reviewed on the weekly call until closed
Owners mark items done or blocked; nothing closes silently
Priorities and tasks, like the current shared sheet but built into the app
A "US Ops HQ" tab in the app for the US Ops team: the to-do tracker, the task grid and the playbook in one place

tracking.agenda_title: Weekly US Ops meeting (30 min): proposed agenda

agenda.t: 24 hrs before: Everyone posts their check-in in the Tracker: what got done, what you're working on now, any roadblocks or risks. The lead reads them before the call
0-3 min: One win: a chapter or teammate shout-out, led by a different person each week
3-15 min: Overdue and blocked: only the items flagged in the Tracker. The owner gives a new date or names what they need
15-25 min: One decision: a single topic picked in advance and framed as a question, led by whoever raised it
25-30 min: Commitments: each person says what they own next week. The Tracker is updated live
After: Recap posted, with an owner and a date on every action item
